title: The evolving landscape of neuroscience

paper.authors: Mario Senden (Department of Cognitive Neuroscience, Maastricht University), single author
paper.venue: Aperture Neuro 6, Issue SI 2 (2026), review article; earlier bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.02.13.638094
paper.repo_license: MIT, (c) 2025 Cognitive Computational Neuroscience Group Maastricht
paper.other_artifacts: Dataset NeuroScape 1.0.1 on Zenodo, doi 10.5281/zenodo.14865161 (not downloaded for this card; contents not verified). Non-OpenAI components: Voyage AI embeddings, a custom PyTorch domain-embedding network, faiss, python-igraph, leidenalg.

dependence.note: Every semantic result (cluster titles and descriptions, the nine research dimensions, emerging and declining trends, open questions) is an LLM-assigned label over article abstracts, so the reported percentages are properties of the annotator's output. The bibliometric layer (counts, growth rates, citation graph, Krackhardt coefficients) is LLM-free and would survive on its own.

claim.statement: Characterising all 175 semantic clusters of 461,316 neuroscience abstracts along nine research dimensions with gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (250 abstracts nearest each cluster centroid per call), the field appears predominantly experimental (96% of clusters) and hypothesis-driven (77%) / data-driven (67%), with only 3% of clusters developing or critiquing theory and only 17% employing overarching theoretical frameworks, while translational (55%) and clinical (30%) work sits atop a broad fundamental base (81%) and 82% of clusters score high or very high on interdisciplinarity (Figure 3a; Sec. Results).
claim.metric: Share of the 175 clusters assigned to each (non-mutually-exclusive) category of the nine LLM-rated dimensions, in percent; downstream, the Matthews phi coefficients between category pairs (Figure 3b) with t-tests on 173 degrees of freedom.
claim.original_source: Paper Figure 3a (quantitative overview of how many clusters qualify for each category) with the percentages restated in the Results text; Figure 3b and the accompanying t statistics; Methods section LLM-BASED ANALYSES for the procedure; cluster count and corpus size from the Results.

protocol.model: none callable - the claim-bearing model is gpt-4o-2024-08-06, which is not in our target snapshot list (target_models.json has no 2024-08-06 entry) and is treated as dead under the project date rule. The only retiring snapshot the paper names, o1-2024-12-17, was used solely to polish the manuscript's language.
protocol.model_status: blocked. gpt-4o-2024-08-06: not callable / out of scope. o1-2024-12-17: dying (shutdown 2026-10-23) but attached to no result.
protocol.model_usage_verified: yes, both statements are explicit. Methods: the semantic analyses were conducted with OpenAI's gpt-4o-2024-08-06 via LangChain (langchain 0.3.19, langchain_openai 0.3.6), and config/analysis/semantic.toml in the repo sets model_name = gpt-4o-2024-08-06, temperature = 1.0. Declaration of Generative AI: o1 (o1-2024-12-17) was used to enhance the article's language and readability.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions through langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI (scripts/semantic_analysis/*.py), JSON output parsed by SimpleJsonOutputParser
protocol.prompt_source: Prompt templates are hardcoded in scripts/semantic_analysis/{cluster_definition,cluster_distinction,assess_dimensions,assess_dimension_categories,extract_trends,extract_open_questions}.py and reprinted verbatim in the paper's Methods; required output fields are listed in config/analysis/semantic.toml

params.note: temperature 1.0 with a single pass per cluster: the label assignment is stochastic and no repeat-agreement figure is reported

protocol.prompt_source_note: The dimension call sends the cluster title plus up to 250 abstracts; the definition call sends up to 200 abstracts; trends compare an older (<=2010) and a recent (>=2021) block of up to 200 abstracts each
protocol.n_items_note: 175 clusters per semantic script; the definition, distinction, dimensions, dimension-categories, trends and open-questions steps are six separate passes over that set
protocol.evaluation: No accuracy metric: the LLM's labels are the measurement. The published numbers are counts over categories, so a re-execution measures annotator stability, not correctness; the repository has no agreement or validation script and the paper reports no inter-rater or repeat-run check.

artifacts.prompts_path: scripts/semantic_analysis/cluster_definition.py, cluster_distinction.py, assess_dimensions.py, assess_dimension_categories.py, extract_trends.py, extract_open_questions.py (prompt templates inline); config/analysis/semantic.toml (model, temperature, required fields, abstract caps)
artifacts.data_path: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14865161 (NeuroScape 1.0.1); the repo carries only code and config. Abstracts are PubMed-derived and the intermediate CSVs (articles_merged_cleaned_filtered_clustered.csv, clusters_defined.csv) are produced by the pipeline, not committed.
artifacts.eval_path: notebooks/results_00_nutshell.ipynb, results_01_clusters.ipynb, results_02_dimensions.ipynb, results_03_growth_trends.ipynb (figure and table construction, including Figure 3a/3b)
artifacts.data_license: code MIT; article CC BY 4.0; the Zenodo dataset's licence was not verified (record not downloaded). PubMed abstracts carry publisher-specific terms.
artifacts.redistributable: code yes; abstract text only under its original publisher terms
artifacts.notes: The pipeline is unusually complete for a single-author review (scraping through figures), but the LLM steps sit at the end of a long chain: Voyage AI embeddings, a trained discipline classifier, a trained domain-embedding network and Leiden clustering all precede them, and each is stochastic. Reproducing Figure 3a therefore requires either the released intermediate clustering or a re-run of the whole chain.

blockers: Dead snapshot: the claim-bearing model gpt-4o-2024-08-06 is outside the callable target set (no 2024-08-06 entry in target_models.json), so the LLM-derived numbers have no live arm.
The only retiring snapshot the paper names, o1-2024-12-17, was used to improve the manuscript's language, not to produce any result - a declaration-only usage that carries no measurable claim.
No ground truth: the nine dimensions are LLM judgements with no human-labelled reference, no repeat-run agreement and no validation set, so a re-run can only measure annotator stability.

Upstream stochasticity: the 175 clusters come from Voyage AI embeddings plus a trained domain network plus Leiden community detection; without the exact released intermediates the cluster identity itself changes, and the percentages are defined over clusters.

Scale and cost: the dimensions step alone sends up to 250 abstracts per cluster (about 82k input tokens per call), so a single full pass over the six semantic scripts is tens of millions of input tokens.

baseline_alive.purpose: no live arm - gpt-4o-2024-08-06 is not callable in this project and o1-2024-12-17 produced no result. The card is filed for the census (dependence type annotator, strength core), not for execution.

successors: gpt-5.6-sol (vendor-designated replacement for both gpt-4o and o1 on the OpenAI deprecations page)
arms.hypothetical_design: If the user wants a successor-annotator arm, the cheapest informative slice is the dimensions step alone on a stratified sample of clusters (for example 30 of 175), scoring category agreement against the published Supplementary Table 3 labels rather than against Figure 3a's aggregate.

pricing_usd_per_1m.note: not applicable - no callable snapshot for the claim

budget.assumptions: Blocked, so no spend is planned. For scale only: an abstract is about 330 tokens, so the dimensions pass is 175 calls x ~82k tokens = about 14.4M input tokens, the definition pass about 11.6M, and trends about 23M; a full single pass over the six semantic scripts is roughly 60M input tokens, i.e. about USD 150 at gpt-4o-2024-08-06 list prices (USD 2.5/1M) or about USD 300 at gpt-4o-2024-05-13 prices. The 30-cluster dimensions slice would be about USD 12.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 cannot be applied: with no callable snapshot for the claim-bearing model there is no baseline_alive result to compare against, so the card is recorded as blocked rather than judged. If a successor-annotator arm is ever approved, the rule would be: hold the released clustering fixed, re-label the same clusters, and judge the direction of the headline contrast (experimental >> theory-developing; overarching frameworks a small minority) with the per-category share as secondary; survival = the 96% / 3% / 17% ordering preserved and each headline share inside a bootstrap CI over clusters, death = the theory-developing share rising to the level of the experimental share, which would mean the label distribution was an annotator artifact.
judgment.notes: This paper is the clean example of a census category we should report: an LLM used as an annotator at the end of a long non-LLM pipeline, with the snapshot named precisely, the prompts published, the code public and the claim still unreproducible because the snapshot is gone. The declaration-only o1 usage is also worth counting separately: full-text snapshot matching finds o1-2024-12-17 here, but the model touched only the prose.

domain_notes: A single-author bibliometric review of 461,316 PubMed abstracts (1999-2023): Voyage AI embeddings, a trained discipline classifier, a domain-specific embedding network and Leiden clustering produce 175 clusters, after which gpt-4o-2024-08-06 supplies every semantic layer (titles, descriptions, nine research dimensions, trends, open questions). The headline conclusions - a predominantly experimental field, only 3% of clusters developing theory, fundamental research at risk of decline, high cross-fertilisation - rest on those LLM labels, with no human-labelled validation. Tier B triage had already marked the paper ineligible (blocker no_number) because the o1 mention is editorial; this card records the stronger reason as well, namely that the claim-bearing snapshot is out of reach, and documents what an executable version would cost.
